title: ChatGPT Health Opens to Everyone in the US
hook: OpenAI is letting anyone in the US plug their medical records into ChatGPT — and claiming its models now reason 'better than clinician level.' That's a big claim to take on trust.
key_points: OpenAI rolled out ChatGPT Health to everyone in the US, per The Verge.
It lets you connect medical records and health-tracking data to the chatbot.
OpenAI health VP Ashley Alexander said its models reason at levels 'better than clinician level.'
That's the company's own claim, made in a briefing — not an independent study.
Connecting records means handing your most sensitive data to a chatbot company.
A chatbot that sounds like a doctor still isn't one, and can still be confidently wrong.
content_html: OpenAI is putting a health assistant in front of the whole US. The Verge reports that ChatGPT Health rolled out to everyone in the country, letting people connect their medical records and health-tracking information so the chatbot can answer questions with your actual history in view.
extra_html:
The eye-catching part is the claim attached to it. In a briefing, OpenAI's vice president of health product, Ashley Alexander, said the company's models "are now capable of reasoning at levels that are better than clinician level." Notice who is speaking: that's the company describing its own product, not an independent study or a regulator. Claims like that are testable in principle, and the useful habit is to wait for someone other than the vendor to test them.

Two things are worth holding at once. A tool that can read your records and explain them in plain language is genuinely useful — most people leave appointments with questions they only think of later. But the same tool is a private company you've just handed your most sensitive data, and a chatbot that sounds authoritative can still be confidently wrong. Use it to understand and to prepare questions; leave the diagnosing to the person who can examine you.

related.title: Asking AI About Health
related.hook: AI beats frantic late-night symptom-googling for calm, readable explanations — and makes a great prep tool for a doctor's visit. What it can't do is examine you or diagnose you.

related.title: AI in Healthcare
related.hook: AI can spot a tumor on a scan faster than a tired radiologist and flag patterns no one would catch by eye. It's a powerful assistant to doctors — not a replacement for one.

related.title: When AI Makes Things Up
related.hook: AI 'hallucinations' aren't glitches — they're the technology working as designed. A model that always predicts a plausible next word will sometimes produce a plausible falsehood.

related.title: When an AI Company Promises a Medical Miracle
related.hook: Midjourney, famous for AI art, now pitches a spa-like water tank that scans your body 'as powerful as an MRI' — but The Verge says the bold claims lack the evidence to back them.

flashcards.prompt: What does ChatGPT Health let people in the US do?

choices.text: Connect their medical records and health-tracking data to the chatbot
Book appointments with a licensed doctor through OpenAI
Get prescriptions filled directly from a chat window

flashcards.explanation_html: The Verge reports the rollout lets more people link medical records and health-tracking information to ChatGPT — not that it replaces a clinic.

flashcards.prompt: Who said OpenAI's models reason 'better than clinician level' — and why does that matter?
flashcards.back_html: OpenAI's own VP of health product, Ashley Alexander, in a company briefing. It's a vendor claim, not an independent result — worth treating as marketing until tested.

flashcards.prompt: What's the main privacy tradeoff in connecting your records to a health chatbot?

choices.text: Your most sensitive personal data now sits with a chatbot company
Your doctor loses access to your own medical history
Nothing changes — medical records aren't personal data

flashcards.explanation_html: Linking records hands a private company your health history. That's a real cost to weigh against the convenience, separate from whether the answers are any good.
